body:
Quick gate result for PR #1952, head ae2620c15cb0aaf34ef56d7bd6dc620655c91ff4.

Commands, run in a new worktree of this head:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run`
- `cargo test -p xtask -j 6`

Why not the full quick gate: the dry run selects 33 steps. Most of them build the camcraft-post and camcraft-app suites. The change touches xtask, and a new worktree needs a full build of those crates. This did not fit the 30 minute budget. The run used `cargo test -p xtask -j 6` instead.

Result of `cargo test -p xtask -j 6`:
- unit tests (xtask, src/main.rs): pass, 141 passed, 0 failed
- tests/merge_ready_skill.rs: pass, 3 passed, 0 failed
- tests/review_artifacts.rs: pass, 3 passed, 0 failed

Dry run: 33 steps in the quick plan, and the plan has one step for each test binary (for example one step per post suite and per app suite, plus the xtask unit tests). The dry run was ok for all 33 steps. The plan steps themselves did not run.

The timing comparison against the old gate was not measured.

Quick pass on head ae2620c15cb0aaf34ef56d7bd6dc620655c91ff4: merges cleanly with main; the quick gate is green on this head (xtask 141 passed; step_tests release_runs_every_target_of_every_crate_one_step_each, batch_runs_lib_and_each_non_slow_binary_one_step_each, only_and_failed_select_one_binary_step; the full quick plan did not run, as the author comment states); the body is complete. The PR is ready for the independent review.

Head ae2620c15c. Verdict: needs changes before merge. The review found one blocker. The rest of the change is sound.

## What I ran (local review worktree, cargo -j 4)
- `cargo test -p xtask`: pass. 141 lib tests, 3 merge_ready_skill tests, 3 review_artifacts tests, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`: 1 step ("xtask unit tests"). Correct for this diff.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`: 713 steps. Step 01 is the debug build; step 02 is "geometry suites: lib". Matches the body.
- `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`: 911 steps. Matches the body.
- Trial merge with `origin/main` (ce59ef446): clean.
- Not run: a full batch or release gate. A full batch is about 40 min here; the post-merge gate on main covers the suites. I did not launch the GUI or any non-test exe.
- Read, not built: the diff adds no file under `.github/` or `scripts/`. I read `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` and the three workflows for step-name coupling.

## What looks good
- The per-binary step pattern copies the heavy-lane mechanism (#1714): one step per cargo selector, own log, own time. Step names, log stems, `--only` and `--failed` work with the colon names; `step_tests::only_and_failed_select_one_binary_step` pins that.
- Batch and release keep the old target coverage. `step_tests` pins the target set for every real crate. `lanes.rs` groups waves by args, not names, so release waves behave as before.
- `post-merge-report.sh` reads the FAIL notes (cargo's `Running tests/<name>.rs` lines), not step names. The rename does not break it. No workflow adds a trigger or runs on a PR event.
- The body has `Process change: yes` and no `PROCESS_VERSION` edit. It has the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1941`. The decision file follows the docs/decisions format.
- Honest exit codes: every step records its cargo exit code; the summary returns 1 when any step failed; a moved checkout returns 1 as VOID.

## Requested before merge
1. `xtask/src/quick.rs:348-354` silently drops a compile check. The build step is suppressed when a crate plans exactly one run step (`targets.len() + fn_steps.len() != 1`). When another binary of that crate has only skipped heavy-lane fns, that binary is in the build list but no step builds it. Example: the diff changes one plain test fn in `crates/app/tests/a.rs` and one `#[ignore]`d fn in `crates/app/tests/b.rs`. Quick runs the fn step for a and never compiles b. The old code always compiled it with the `build-only (changed fns are heavy lane)` step, and the new comment at quick.rs:329-331 says the same. Suggested change: suppress the build step only when the one run step covers every binary in the build list. Please add a pinning test for the two-binary shape; the current fixture cases (tests.rs:100) use one binary for both changes, so no test holds the line.

## Notes (not blocking)
- `xtask/src/quick.rs` is now 401 lines. The ~400-line rule asks for a split at the next touch.
- A batch or release `--dry-run` now takes minutes: the checkout guard calls git once per step (713 calls). A dry run could skip the guard. This could ride on #1951 or get one P7 row.
- When the batch build step fails, the 712 later steps still run and each fails on the same compile error. The release path breaks the waves after a failed build (exec.rs:171); the sequential path could do the same.
- The +6 min serial estimate for batch (body) is not measured on the Linux runner. The first post-merge run will show it against the 20 min target; watch it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Review cost: effort:medium (issue #1941). No escalation. Built and tested locally at head ae2620c15 (xtask suites green); one blocker posted in the review comment; PR set needs-rework and back to draft.

Review fixes on new head 3dbd6f26f3c5f574a8822e9b680bbfa7a9541dac (one commit after ae2620c15, plain push).

Findings and results:
- Blocker (`xtask/src/quick.rs`, build step dropped): fixed. Quick now skips the crate build step only when the one run step covers the one target of the build list. New pinning test `tests::heavy_fn_in_a_second_binary_keeps_the_build_step`: a plain fn changes in `cmds`, a heavy fn changes in `ops`. The plan has `app build (--no-run) ... --test ops --test cmds`, then the `cmds` fn step. The test fails on ae2620c15 (no build step) and passes on the new head.
- Note 1 (401 lines): fixed. `xtask/src/quick.rs` has 398 lines.
- Note 2 (slow dry run): fixed. A dry run does not read the checkout for each step. `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` plans 713 steps in about 1 s.
- Note 3 (batch continues after a failed build): fixed. The sequential path stops after a failed `debug build (--no-run)` step, as the release waves do. The step name is now the constant `plan::DEBUG_BUILD`. The per-crate quick builds do not stop the other crates. The batch case is added to `lanes_tests::release_executor_overlaps_lanes_and_keeps_failure_and_checkout_guards`.
- Note 4 (batch time on the Linux runner): not changed. Only the first post-merge run can measure it.

Gate on the new head:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1 step, xtask unit tests, pass (142 passed, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: a full batch or release gate.

The PR stays a draft. The review labels stay with the reviewer.

Head 3dbd6f26f. Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

## Status of the earlier findings (review at ae2620c15)
- Blocker (quick dropped the build step when one fn step did not cover the build list): fixed. `xtask/src/quick.rs:352` now suppresses the build step only when the build list has one target (`units == 1`) and one run step covers it. The new test `tests::heavy_fn_in_a_second_binary_keeps_the_build_step` uses the two-binary shape (a plain fn in `cmds`, a heavy fn in `ops`). It passes on this head.
- Note 1 (quick.rs was 401 lines): fixed. It has 398 lines.
- Note 2 (a dry run read the checkout per step): fixed. `xtask/src/exec.rs:216` returns early for a dry run. Measured here: `gate batch --dry-run` plans 766 steps in 0.97 s; `gate release --dry-run` plans 978 steps in 1.26 s.
- Note 3 (batch continued after a failed build step): fixed. The sequential path stops when the `plan::DEBUG_BUILD` step fails (`xtask/src/exec.rs:200`). `lanes_tests::release_executor_overlaps_lanes_and_keeps_failure_and_checkout_guards` pins the batch case. It passes.
- Note 4 (batch time on the Linux runner): not measured, as the author states. Follow-up #1951 exists.

## Requested before merge
None.

## What I ran (local review worktree, merged with origin/main, cargo -j 4)
- Trial merge with `origin/main` (1f15f98e7): clean. GitHub reports MERGEABLE.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: `test result: FAILED. 147 passed; 1 failed` (bin); `merge_ready_skill` 3 passed; `review_artifacts` 3 passed. The one failure is not from this PR - see below.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `Finished dev profile`, no warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run`: 766 steps. Step 01 is `debug build (--no-run)`. Steps are `<crate> suites: lib`, `<crate> suites: <binary>`, and `ui suites: bins` / `ui suites: doc`. The ui steps keep cwd `crates/ui`.
- `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`: 978 steps, heavy lanes included (`motion heavy: lib`, ...).
- Not run: a full batch or release tier; a real gate run; the GUI. Only dry runs and the xtask suites.

## One failure is not from this PR
- `gate_maps_tests::no_gate_map_names_a_moved_module_as_app` fails with `suites without a Gate map: ["post_script_options"]`.
- The suite `crates/app/tests/post_script_options.rs` came from main (ec8fd4b06, #258). It has no Gate map line. The test function is identical in main and in this head; this PR does not change it. The test therefore fails on `origin/main` alone. It is a main problem, not a problem of this PR.

## Process law
- The diff changes process files (`xtask/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`). The body carries the line `Process change: yes`. The diff does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. Pass.
- The tier table, the gate skill and the xtask usage text describe the same steps. The wrappers `scripts/gate.ps1` and `scripts/gate.sh` are not in the diff; their `gate <tier>` forwarding is unchanged.

## Judgement against the gate law
- Quick: one step for each touched test target, and one crate build when the crate has more than one run step. No heavy lanes. This fits the 5 min target.
- Batch: one build step, then one step for each debug target minus `SLOW_BINARIES`; ui keeps lib, bins, every binary and doc, as its old single whole-crate step did. `step_tests` pins the target set for every crate. The body estimate (about 6 min more serial time) must be watched against the 20 min target on the first post-merge run.
- Release: one step for each debug target and the heavy lanes. The waves in `lanes.rs` are unchanged.
- `--only "app suites: lib"` and `--failed` pick one colon-name step; `step_tests::only_and_failed_select_one_binary_step` pins it.

## Notes (not blocking)
- Batch does not run the xtask self-tests, before or after this change. That is one reason the main failure above stayed hidden. A `source:agent` row for it may be worth it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
